Negative values would produce invalid SQL (OFFSET/LIMIT must be non-negative in PostgreSQL) raising ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid and returning a 500 instead of a 4xx for malformed input. The mechanism is verifiable from the diff; severity is modest but it is a real defect introduced by this change.

judged_text: members passes params[:offset].to_i and (params[:limit] || 50).to_i straight into .offset()/.limit() with no validation, so negative values reach SQL as OFFSET -1 / LIMIT -1. GET /groups/{name}/members.json?offset=-1 makes PostgreSQL raise its 'must not be negative' error as ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid and the request returns a raw 500 instead of a 4xx for the malformed parameter.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, then directly calls `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no guard against negative values, so `offset=-1` becomes `OFFSET -1` in SQL, which PostgreSQL rejects (raising an exception and likely producing a 500). This behavior is newly applied to all groups (previously pagination was only applied for `group.automatic?`).
